q: 1. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest division of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernire scale divided by total number of division of primary scale
explain: Least count of a vernier = (value of one main scale division) / (total number of divisions on the vernier scale); this is the smallest reading directly obtainable with the vernier.

q: 2. On a diagonal scale, it is possible to read up to
explain: A diagonal scale uses primary divisions, sub-divisions, and diagonal lines to allow three successive dimensions to be read directly, e.g. units, tenths and hundredths.

q: 3. If h is the difference in height between end points of a chain of length l, the required slope correction is
explain: Slope correction Cs = h2/(2l), derived from the approximation of the difference between the slope distance and horizontal distance for small slope angles.

q: 4. A tape of length l and weight 'w' kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of P kg, the sag correction is,
explain: The standard sag correction formula for a tape hanging in a catenary between supports is Cs = L*W2/(24P2) per span, where W = w*L is the total weight of the span.

q: 5. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to
explain: Accidental errors tend to partly cancel each other, so their cumulative effect over a distance L grows in proportion to the square root of L, not L itself.

q: 6. While measuring a chain line between two stations intervened by a raised ground
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: A raised ground (hillock) between two intervisible-but-blocked stations obstructs the line of sight between them, while the chain can still be laid along the ground; hence only vision is obstructed.

q: 7. In chain surveying tie lines are primarily provided
options: to check the accuracy of the survey
to take offsets for detail survey
to avoid long offsets from chain lines
to increase the number of chain lines
explain: Tie lines join subsidiary points on the main survey lines so that offsets to detail near them remain short and manageable, avoiding the errors of very long offsets.

q: 8. In chain surveying field work is limited to
explain: Chain surveying uses only a chain/tape for measuring distances; no angle-measuring instrument is employed, so the field work involves linear measurements only.

q: 9. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than
explain: A well-conditioned triangle keeps all its angles between 30 deg and 120 deg so that a small error in angle measurement causes only a small error in the plotted position of the point.

q: 10. A plain scale is used to read
explain: A plain scale has only primary and secondary divisions, allowing two dimensions (e.g., units and tenths, such as metres and decimetres) to be read directly.

q: 11. Chain surveying is well adopted for
explain: Chain surveying works best for small, fairly open areas with simple details, since it depends only on linear measurements which are easiest to take without obstructions.

q: 12. The angle between two plane mirrors of optical square, is
explain: An optical square uses two mirrors inclined at 45 deg to each other, which by the double-reflection principle deviates a ray of light through 90 deg, enabling right angles to be set out.

q: 13. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is
explain: For very short offsets, about 5 m or less, sufficient accuracy in setting the right angle can be achieved by judging perpendicularity with the eye alone.

q: 14. When the length of chain used in measuring distance is longer than the standard length, the error in measured distance will be ...............
explain: If the chain is too long, it measures a shorter distance than actual, resulting in a negative error (Correction is positive).

q: 15. For indirect ranging, number of ranging rods required, is
explain: Indirect (reciprocal) ranging is used when the end stations are not intermutually visible and requires two ranging rods held by two assistants plus one at each end station, i.e., four rods in total.

q: 16. A clinometer is used for
explain: A clinometer is a simple instrument used to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground.

q: 17. Short offsets are measured with:
explain: A) **an ordinary chain**: For very short offsets (usually under 15m), an ordinary chain or even a simple offset rod is sufficient and faster than using a precision tape.

q: 18. Greater accuracy in linear measurements, is obtained by ...............
explain: Invar tapes have a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making them the most accurate for baseline measurements.

q: 19. It is more difficult to obtain good results while measuring horizontal distance by stepping ...............
explain: Stepping uphill is harder because the person at the front must maintain alignment and plumbing while looking 'up' the slope.

q: 20. Number of links per meter length of a chain are
explain: A metric chain has links of 0.2 m each, so there are 5 links per metre length of the chain.

q: 21. Cross-staff is used for
explain: A cross-staff is a simple optical instrument with two pairs of slits/mirrors set at right angles to each other, used for setting out perpendicular offsets (right angles) in chain surveying.

q: 22. Invar tapes are made of an alloy of:
explain: A) **nickel and steel**: Invar consists of 36% nickel and 64% steel. Its extremely low coefficient of thermal expansion makes it ideal for precise baseline measurements.

q: 23. Cross staff is an instrument used for ...............
explain: A cross-staff is a simple instrument used in chain surveying to set out perpendicular offsets (right angles) from the chain line.

q: 24. Normal tension is that pull which ...............
options: is used at the time of standardizing the tape
neutralizes the effect due to pull and sag
makes the correction due to sag equal to zero
makes the correction due to pull equal to zero
explain: Normal tension is the specific amount of pull where the positive correction for pull exactly equals the negative correction for sag.

q: 25. Which of the following is not used in measuring perpendicular offsets?
explain: A line ranger is used to establish intermediate points on a straight line, not for measuring perpendicular offsets.

q: 26. Which of the following instrument is generally used for base line measurements?
explain: Invar tapes are used for primary baseline measurements because their low thermal expansion ensures high precision.

q: 27. An invar tape is made of an alloy of ...............
explain: Invar is an alloy consisting of approximately 36% nickel and 64% steel.

q: 28. Ranging is the process of ...............
options: fixing ranging rods on the extremities of area
aligning the chain in a straight line between two extremities
taking offsets from a chain line
chaining over a range of mountains
explain: Ranging is the operation of establishing intermediate points on a straight line between two distant fixed stations.

q: 29. In chain surveying, perpendiculars to the chain line, are set out by
explain: In chain surveying, right angles (perpendicular offsets) to the chain line are set out using simple instruments like the optical square (or cross staff), not a theodolite or level.

q: 30. Ranging in chain survey means
options: looking at an isolated point not on the line
establishing an intermediate point on the line
determining the distance between and points
explain: Ranging is the process of establishing intermediate points on a straight line between two end stations so that the chain can be laid out straight.

q: 31. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operation are due to
explain: Systematic errors that follow a definite, regular pattern typically arise from faulty or improperly adjusted instruments, rather than random human lapses.

q: 32. Which one of the following mistakes/errors may be cumulative positive or negative?
explain: The error due to sag in a tape is always cumulative and in one fixed direction (negative, i.e., measured length is too long) for a given tension and support condition -- however per key, sag is identified as the answer among mistakes that can be cumulative positive or negative depending on set-up.

q: 33. Ceylon Ghat tracer can read slopes up to ...............
explain: The Ceylon Ghat Tracer is a simple instrument used for setting out gradients, typically ranging from 1 in 6 to 1 in 120.

q: 34. An instrument used for ranging is
explain: A line ranger is an optical instrument specifically used to fix intermediate points on a straight line between two end stations, i.e., for ranging.

q: 35. An open cross-staff is commonly used for setting out ...............
explain: While cross-staffs are for right angles, the 'open' type is often utilized for relatively longer offsets compared to simple chain offsets.

q: 36. A chain may get elongated due to
explain: Repeated use causes wear at the joints and the rings/links open out slightly, which is the main cause of permanent elongation of a chain (as opposed to temporary changes from temperature or pull).

q: 37. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is ...............
explain: The two mirrors of an optical square are fixed at an angle of 45° to reflect rays through 90°.

q: 38. Handles of chains are made up of
explain: The handles of a surveying chain are usually made of brass (a non-magnetic, corrosion resistant material), while the links themselves are of steel or galvanized iron.

q: 39. The horizontal glass in an optical square is ...............
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The horizon glass is half-silvered so the observer can see one signal directly and the other by reflection.

q: 40. The length of an Engineer's chain is
explain: An Engineer's chain is 100 feet long, divided into 100 links of 1 foot each, distinguishing it from Gunter's chain (66 feet).

q: 41. The index glass in an optical square is ...............
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The index glass is completely silvered to ensure a strong reflection of the object onto the horizon glass.

q: 42. Drop arrow is used in
explain: In the method of stepping (used for measuring distances on sloping ground), a drop arrow is used at each step to mark the point on the ground vertically below the end of the horizontal tape segment.

q: 43. The instrument, belonging to a class of reflecting instrument is ...............
explain: All these instruments use the principles of reflection (mirrors or prisms) to align sights or read scales.

q: 44. In an optical square, the angle between the first incident ray and the last reflected ray is ...............
explain: The geometry of an optical square is specifically designed to result in a 90° deviation between the original ray and the final reflected ray.

q: 45. When a chain encounters a river
options: chaining is obstructed but ranging is free
ranging is obstructed but chaining is free
both ranging and chaining are obstructed
both ranging and chaining are free
explain: When a river lies between two chain stations, the chain cannot be physically laid across the water (chaining obstructed), but the line of sight across the river remains clear (ranging free).

q: 46. When the object lies on the left hand side of the chain line, then while taking offset with an optical square, it is held in ...............
explain: To view an object on the left through the reflection while staying on the line, holding it upright in the right hand is the standard procedure.

q: 47. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a line are not mutually visible due to a hillock (raised ground) in between, obstructing the direct line of sight.

q: 48. Check lines (or proof lines) in Chain Surveying are essentially required ...............
options: to indicate the accuracy of the survey work
explain: Check lines are measured to verify the accuracy of the framework and plotting; if the check line distance matches the plot, the work is correct.

q: 49. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is ...............
explain: A clinometer is specifically designed to measure angles of slope, elevation, or depression.

q: 50. An instrument that can be used as an optical square is
explain: A box sextant is a compact instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles. It can be used to set out right angles, making it a versatile alternative to the optical square.
